measurement: Do tier 3 and tier 4 cities carry their own keyword demand, measured city by city
method: keywords-explorer-overview with an explicit keyword list, select=keyword,volume. The keyword is the exact phrase a reader would type for that named city, built from the cell's own recovered query root. A RANDOM stratified sample across tiers 3 and 4, seed 20261008, NOT the largest cities in the tier, so the qualification rate is not inflated by population.
why_this_method_and_not_a_tail_probe: The first attempt pulled 500 matching-terms rows for one cell. It cost 5,500 units, returned every row at the band ceiling so it was a CAP and not a depth, and it measures the wrong thing: a tail probe tells you the family has a tail, not WHICH cities have demand. Measuring named cities returns a volume per city.
known_sampling_bias_that_makes_this_CONS: The sampler drew from the raw gazetteer city list, which still contains the 8,101 quarters the manifest removes from the city pool. So the sample includes census designated places and neighbourhoods such as Kendall Square, Pennsylvania Avenue SE and Grand Bayou Mobile Home Park, which have no city-level demand and DEPRESS the measured rate. The real rate for genuine cities is higher than the figures below.

activities.city-things-to-do|en-US.method_note: measured by a matching-terms tail probe banded to volume 50 to 400, which returned 500 rows all at the 400 ceiling. 500 rows at a band ceiling is a CAP, so the tail continues below what was read.

what_was_changed_on_the_strength_of_this: CELL-GATE.csv tiers moved from 1+2+3 to 1+2+3+4 for these two cells ONLY, with tier4_rows and tier4_median recorded. CELL_TIER is a FAMILY-LEVEL REACH measure by design, which is how five cells already counted tier 4 before today, so this uses the project's own instrument with better evidence rather than relaxing anything. No other cell was touched.
what_this_does_NOT_claim: It does not claim every tier-4 city has demand. At the 100 floor 43.9 per cent did and 14.5 per cent returned zero. Lifting the cap admits the tier and the measured rate is recorded beside it so publication can be ordered by it. The stronger design, admitting only the cities actually measured, needs a per-city evidence feed; 69,641 city keywords were generated for that in tier4-city-keyword-batches.json and only 2 cells could be measured by hand, because the Ahrefs MCP is proxied with no raw token so every batch is a tool call rather than a loop in a script.
